claims_control: External resource estimates, measured QEC evidence, and vendor roadmaps only; no production key break is claimed. Cross-architecture physical-qubit extrapolation is prohibited without a complete fault-tolerant overhead model, and roadmap targets are never treated as demonstrated capability.

attack_estimates.name: Google Quantum AI 2026 low-width secp256k1 ECDLP
attack_estimates.runtime_note: Published superconducting scenario says minutes with fewer than 500,000 physical qubits under stated assumptions; no exact runtime is encoded here.

attack_estimates.name: IonQ Walking Cat trapped-ion secp256k1 ECDLP
attack_estimates.runtime_note: 25.7 days per attempt under the published Walking Cat architecture assumptions.

attack_estimates.name: Luo et al. 2026 space-efficient complete ECDLP
attack_estimates.runtime_note: 835 logical qubits is a complete Shor/ECDLP width result. The stored Toffoli value is the 919*n^3/log2(n) leading term evaluated at n=256; the paper also includes O(n^2). Do not infer fast runtime without architecture-specific compilation.

hardware_roadmaps.claims_note: Forward-looking vendor target only. It is 35 logical qubits below the Luo 835-qubit width result and far below the published Walking Cat physical/width envelope. No attack capability is inferred.

Forward-looking vendor target only. The target numerically overlaps IonQ's published Walking Cat attack envelope of about 19,397 physical and about 1,450 logical qubits. This is a migration-planning trigger, not evidence that the target will be achieved or that the attack will execute as modeled.

qec_evidence.name: Quantinuum C4-Helix on Helios
qec_evidence.claims_note: Hardware validates compact logical memory, Clifford computation and heterogeneous-code entanglement without postselection. The 10:1 code-block ratio must NOT be multiplied by an ECDLP logical-qubit estimate and reported as complete attack hardware. Full non-Clifford resources, factories/ancillas, routing, decoding, runtime reliability, scaling and attack-specific compilation are not established by this experiment.

roadmap_collision_policy.purpose: Detect when a forward hardware roadmap numerically reaches a published attack envelope early enough to threaten migration schedules.
roadmap_collision_policy.hard_rule: A roadmap collision may increase migration urgency but never establishes Q2, Q3, Q4, Q-day, or a demonstrated production break.
roadmap_collision_policy.current_trigger: IonQ's 2028 roadmap target of 20,000 physical / 1,600 logical qubits numerically overlaps IonQ's own Walking Cat secp256k1 attack estimate of 19,397 physical / about 1,450 logical qubits.
